title: Projective PGL quotient with universal closed images of invariant subschemes
statement: Let $k$ be any field [def-weil-field], $r\geq2$, and $G=\operatorname{PGL}_{r,k}$, the affine group scheme of invertible matrices modulo scalar matrices. Let $Z$ be a projective finite-type $k$-scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-kun-projective, def-weil-finite-type-morphism] with a $G$-action and an ample $G$-linearized invertible module $A$ [def-sc-invertible-module, def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. Linearization and the geometric semistable open subscheme $Z^{ss}(A)$ have the meanings in [lem-sfb-hilbert-plucker-pgl-linearization]. There exist a projective finite-type $k$-scheme $Q$ and a surjective invariant finite-type morphism $q:Z^{ss}(A)\to Q$ which is affine, meaning that the inverse image of every affine open subscheme is affine. Invariant means $q\circ a=q\circ\mathrm{pr}_2$ for the action $a:G\times_kZ^{ss}(A)\to Z^{ss}(A)$. For every scheme $T$ and morphism $T\to Q$, put $X_T=Z^{ss}(A)\times_Q T$ and $G_T=G\times_kT$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. For every closed subscheme $C\hookrightarrow X_T$ [def-weil-closed-immersion] whose defining ideal is preserved by the $G_T$-action, the image of $|C|$ under $X_T\to T$ is closed in $|T|$. The assertions include nonreduced $Z$ and arbitrary characteristic; no linear reductivity or stabilizer hypothesis is assumed.

source.place: Alper, Adequate moduli spaces and geometrically reductive group schemes, published version, introduction pp.490--491 (projective semistable quotient); Theorems 9.1.4 and 9.7.6, finite generation Theorem 6.3.3, and universal closedness Theorem 5.3.1(2), with Proposition 5.2.9(3). Affine invariant charts give affineness of q. Local PDF WANTED; read online.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-ample-very-ample-immersion-affine-base], some $A^{\otimes d}$ is the pullback of $\mathcal O(1)$ under an immersion $i:Z\to\mathbf P^n_k$. The scheme $Z$ is proper by [lem-pc-projective-proper], and $\mathbf P^n_k$ is separated since it is projective and hence proper by the same node. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-proper-to-separated] makes $i$ proper, and [lem-weil-pbc-proper-immersion-closed] makes it a closed immersion. The polarization hypothesis of [lem-sfb-projective-polarization-section-algebra] is now satisfied. Put $S=\bigoplus_{m\geq0}\Gamma(Z,A^{\otimes m})$; that node gives finite generation of $S$ over $k$, finite dimension of every $S_m$, and affine finite-type charts $Z_s=\operatorname{Spec}S_{(s)}$ for all positive-degree homogeneous $s$.

source.place: Introduction, printed pp.490--491, invariant section-ring quotient; agent expansion of the affine-chart construction.

proof.text: Each tensor power of $A$ is locally free of rank one, hence quasi-coherent by [def-sc-invertible-module]. The linearization [def-sfb-pgl-linearized-polarization] induces a degree-preserving rational $G$-action on $S$. Explicitly, pull back each section by $a:G\times Z\to Z$, identify $a^*A$ with $\mathrm{pr}_2^*A$ by the linearization, and use [lem-sc-flat-base-change-coherent] in degree zero with coefficient algebra $k[G]$ to identify the resulting sections with $S_m\otimes_k k[G]$. Flatness holds by [lem-weil-pbc-module-over-field-flat]; properness of $Z$ was proved in step 1. Tensor compatibility gives multiplication compatibility, and the identity and cocycle laws give counit and coassociativity. Put $R=S^G=\bigoplus_m(S_m)^G$. By [lem-sfb-pgl-geometric-reductivity], $R$ is finitely generated. Its degree-zero part is a subspace of the finite-dimensional $S_0$, so [lem-sfb-finite-graded-proj-projective] makes $Q=\operatorname{Proj}R$ projective and of finite type over $k$. This does not assume $R_0=k$.

source.place: Introduction, printed pp.490--491, invariant section-ring quotient; agent expansion of the affine-chart construction.

proof.text: The geometric semistability convention in [lem-sfb-hilbert-plucker-pgl-linearization] is exactly the invariant-section convention in [def-sfb-pgl-linearized-polarization]. The invariant nonvanishing opens $Z_s$, for homogeneous $s\in R_d$, $d>0$, cover $Z^{ss}(A)$ by its defining semistability condition [def-sfb-pgl-linearized-polarization]. This agrees with geometric semistability: apply [lem-sc-flat-base-change-coherent] to an algebraically closed field extension and [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact], with [lem-weil-pbc-module-over-field-flat], to the kernel defining invariants of $S_m$. Explicitly, for an algebraically closed extension $K/k$, tensor the exact sequence $0\to(S_m)^G\to S_m\xrightarrow{\rho-\iota}S_m\otimes_k k[G]$, where $\iota(v)=v\otimes1$, with $K$. The base-change section and coaction identifications give $(S_m)^G\otimes_kK\cong(S_m\otimes_kK)^{G_K}$. A nonzero value of a finite $K$-linear combination of sections from $(S_m)^G$ forces one of those sections to have nonzero value. Thus every geometrically semistable point lies in an invariant nonvanishing open defined over $k$. Every $Z_s$ is $G$-invariant, since the section $s$ is invariant on all test schemes.

source.place: Introduction, printed pp.490--491, invariant section-ring quotient; agent expansion of the affine-chart construction.

proof.text: For $s\in R_d$, $d>0$, set $B_s=S_{(s)}=\Gamma(Z_s,\mathcal O)$ using [lem-sfb-projective-polarization-section-algebra]. Then $(B_s)^G=R_{(s)}$. Here is the denominator argument, including zero divisors: an invariant fraction $a/s^n$, $a\in S_{nd}$, satisfies $\rho(a)-a\otimes1=0$ after inverting $s\otimes1$. Thus some $(s\otimes1)^N$ annihilates this difference, and $s^Na$ is an invariant homogeneous numerator representing the same fraction with denominator $s^{n+N}$. Conversely a fraction with invariant numerator and denominator is invariant. Injectivity follows from the same localization relation in the subring $R\subset S$: $s^Nb=0$ in $S$ is also the identical equality in $R$. The chart isomorphism respects the action because the linearization carries the ratio $a/s^n$ to the ratio of its translates.

source.place: Introduction, printed pp.490--491, invariant section-ring quotient; agent expansion of the affine-chart construction.

proof.text: The inclusion $R_{(s)}\hookrightarrow B_s$ defines an invariant morphism $q_s:Z_s\to D_+(s)\subset Q$ by [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-into-affine-scheme] and [def-pc-proj]. For $t\in R_e$, $e>0$, [lem-weil-pbc-proj-basic-open-intersection] describes $D_+(s)\cap D_+(t)$ inside $D_+(s)$ by invertibility of $t^d/s^e$. Its pullback is the function $t^d/s^e$ on $Z_s$, invertible exactly on $Z_s\cap Z_t$. On this intersection both $q_s$ and $q_t$ send every degree-zero fraction from $R_{(st)}$ to the ratio of the same sections of $A$; they are equal by the affine-target bijection. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing] glues them to $q:Z^{ss}(A)\to Q$. For every $s$, the inverse image $q^{-1}(D_+(s))$ is exactly $Z_s$, by the intersection calculation on the covering $\{Z_t\}$. Equality of action and projection composites holds on these invariant opens, hence globally by that same gluing uniqueness.

source.place: Introduction, printed pp.490--491, invariant section-ring quotient; agent expansion of the affine-chart construction.

proof.text: The equality $q^{-1}(D_+(s))=Z_s$ and [pqf-lem-affine-local-target] show that $q$ is affine. It is also finite type directly from [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Indeed $Z$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] (a field is Noetherian), and every open of $Z$ is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian]. Given any affine $V\subset Q$, cover $q^{-1}(V)$ by principal affine opens inside the affine finite-type charts $Z_s$. Each such coordinate ring is a localization $B_s[1/h]$ and is finitely generated over $k$, hence over $\Gamma(V,\mathcal O)$ through $q$, since the image of that algebra contains $k$. Quasi-compactness gives a finite subcover, which is precisely the finite-type criterion. This argument checks all affine $V$, not just the Proj charts.

source.place: Introduction, printed pp.490--491, invariant section-ring quotient; agent expansion of the affine-chart construction.

proof.text: For each $s$, the rational $G$-algebra $B_s$ is finitely generated over $k$. The group $G$ is smooth affine and of finite type by [lem-sfb-pgl-reductive-structure], and [lem-sfb-pgl-geometric-reductivity] supplies the power-lifting hypothesis for every equivariant surjection of finite-type $G$-algebras. Apply [lem-sfb-power-lifting-adequate-affine-quotient] to obtain an adequate moduli morphism $\phi_s:[Z_s/G]\to\operatorname{Spec}(B_s^G)=D_+(s)$. The canonical smooth surjective atlas $Z_s\to[Z_s/G]$ and its composite with $\phi_s$ are given by [lem-sfb-affine-action-stack-presentation]; the composite is $q_s$. By [lem-sfb-adequate-moduli-universal-closed-topology] with $T=D_+(s)$, $\phi_s$ is surjective. Thus $q_s$ is surjective, and these chartwise surjections prove that $q$ is surjective.

Fix any $T\to Q$ and invariant closed subscheme $C\hookrightarrow X_T$. Work on the open cover $T_s=T\times_QD_+(s)$ of $T$. The atlas of [lem-sfb-affine-action-stack-presentation] is representable by spaces since its target has representable diagonal. Apply [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus] to its base change: $U_s=Z_s\times_{D_+(s)}T_s\to\mathcal X_s=[Z_s/G]\times_{D_+(s)}T_s$ is smooth and surjective. The cited statement defines surjectivity by lifting field-valued objects after field extension, so every point of $|\mathcal X_s|$ comes from $U_s$. By [def-sfb-affine-action-quotient-stack], two such points agree exactly when their trivial torsors become isomorphic after common field extension. Such an isomorphism is translation by a group-valued point over the same $T_s$-point. Membership in $C\cap U_s$ is preserved and reflected by field extension: a field map kills its ideal exactly when the extended map does. Preservation of its ideal under the action gives the same equivalence under translation, using the inverse element for the reverse implication. Thus $|C\cap U_s|$ is saturated. Its image $W_s\subset|\mathcal X_s|$ has inverse image exactly $|C\cap U_s|$ in the smooth atlas, so is closed by the atlas topology in [lem-sfb-adequate-moduli-universal-closed-topology]. Apply that theorem to the adequate morphism $\phi_s$ and the arbitrary map $T_s\to D_+(s)$: the image of $W_s$ in $T_s$ is closed. It equals the image of $C\cap U_s$, hence $q_T(|C|)\cap|T_s|$, since $U_s=q_T^{-1}(T_s)$. Closedness on this open cover proves the assertion. This uses neither flatness of $T_s\to D_+(s)$ nor adequacy of the base-changed morphism.

lean.statement: theorem projective_pgl_invariant_quotient (k : Type u) [Field k] (r : ℕ) (hr : 2 ≤ r) (Z : Over (Spec (.of k))) (hprojective : IsHProjective Z.hom) (hfiniteType : LocallyOfFiniteType Z.hom ∧ QuasiCompact Z.hom) (L : Z.left.Modules) [L.IsInvertible] (hample : Scheme.Modules.IsAmple Z.left L) (D : Action k r Z L) : ∃ U : Z.left.Opens, (∀ (Ω : Type u) [Field Ω] [Algebra k Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω] (x : fieldTest k Ω ⟶ Z), x.left.base (⟨⊥, Ideal.isPrime_bot⟩ : PrimeSpectrum Ω) ∈ U ↔ D.IsSemistable Ω x) ∧ ∃ (Q : Over (Spec (.of k))) (q : Over.mk (U.ι ≫ Z.hom) ⟶ Q), IsHProjective Q.hom ∧ LocallyOfFiniteType Q.hom ∧ QuasiCompact Q.hom ∧ Surjective q.left ∧ LocallyOfFiniteType q.left ∧ QuasiCompact q.left ∧ IsAffineHom q.left ∧ (∀ (W : Over (Spec (.of k))) (g : Matrices k r W) (x y : W ⟶ Over.mk (U.ι ≫ Z.hom)), y ≫ (Over.homMk U.ι : Over.mk (U.ι ≫ Z.hom) ⟶ Z) = D.act W g (x ≫ (Over.homMk U.ι : Over.mk (U.ι ≫ Z.hom) ⟶ Z)) → y ≫ q = x ≫ q) ∧ (∀ (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) (t : T ⟶ Q) (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) (i : C ⟶ pullback q t), IsClosedImmersion i.left → (∀ (W : Over (Spec (.of k))) (g : Matrices k r W) (x : W ⟶ C), ∃ y : W ⟶ C, y ≫ i ≫ pullback.snd q t = x ≫ i ≫ pullback.snd q t ∧ y ≫ i ≫ pullback.fst q t ≫ (Over.homMk U.ι : Over.mk (U.ι ≫ Z.hom) ⟶ Z) = D.act W g (x ≫ i ≫ pullback.fst q t ≫ (Over.homMk U.ι : Over.mk (U.ι ≫ Z.hom) ⟶ Z))) → IsClosed (Set.range (i ≫ pullback.snd q t).left))
